newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev drops to 400 to dlr, new fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev drops to 400 to dlr, new fall seen.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 395-400 per dollar by 1000 local time (0800 GMT) from Tuesday's close at 386-387 due to a rise in foreign currency demand and amid uncertainty caused by a national strike, dealers said.
"As in the past two days large final clients are bidding for large foreign currency volumes but banks are reluctant to sell in anticipation of a new lev fall," a commercial bank delaer said.
Around 0815 GMT the dollar was bid at 400-405 levs and was offered around 425 levs, but no deals were reported above 400, traders said.
"The central bank is not likely to support the lev today and traders are very cautious," another dealer said.

The lev has come under strong pressure from energy importers bidding for foreign currency since the beginning of the week and the BNB has tried to slow down the lev fall but the volumes it sold were too low to meet demand, traders said.
The lev traded at 362-364 per dollar on Monday. @
Dealers said banks were very cautious also due to uncertainty over the outcome of the nationwide strike, which according to witnesses looked more like a token strike by around 0830 GMT.
"The (domestic) market is rarely influenced by political events but this strike may cause strong political destabilisation," a third dealer said.

Bulgaria's biggest trade union organisation has called a nationwide one-day strike for Wednesday to demand a cabinet reshuffle and early parliamentary elections. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
